result.question:
I'm worried that urgent work on Transformer 1 at site MAIN is stuck behind an overloaded technician. Give me the MAIN site's work order KPIs for the last 6 months, including backlog, overdue count and average completion time. Then list every open work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority, scheduled date and assigned technician, and flag which ones are overdue.

For each technician assigned to those work orders, count how many open work orders they currently hold at MAIN. Anyone holding more than 5 counts as overloaded.

Next, work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630.

If Transformer 1 is at Condition 2 or higher, do the following for any overdue work order on it that sits with an overloaded technician. Reassign it to the technician with the fewest open work orders at MAIN, choosing among those who have worked on Transformer 1 before and are not overloaded. Give it a start date within the next 7 days that avoids any day with 3 or more scheduled work orders at MAIN. If it is Condition 1, don't reassign anything. Just list the overdue items and recommend a catch-up order, ranked by priority and then by how late they are.

If every technician with Transformer 1 history is overloaded, don't reassign. Tell me who is least loaded and recommend bringing in outside help. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
result.answer:
Nothing further is needed — every dependency is resolved (KPIs, all MAIN work orders, Transformer 1 history, 7‑day calendar, latest oil sample), so no additional calls are required.

## 1. MAIN site KPIs — last 6 months
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Total work orders | 1 |
| Completed | 0 |
| Backlog | 1 |
| Overdue | 0 |
| Avg completion time | 0 hrs (nothing completed in period) |
| Priority breakdown | P1: 1 |
| Top asset by WO count | Transformer 1 (1) |

## 2. Open work orders on Transformer 1
| WO # | Description | Priority | Status | Scheduled start | Assigned technician | Overdue? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection – on‑load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking); confirmatory oil sample for lab DGA added 2026‑09‑30 | 1 | APPR | **none** (no sched/target dates) | **none** (no labor line) | **Not overdue** — cannot be, as no date has ever been set |

## 3. Technician loads at MAIN (open WOs)
No technician is assigned to any Transformer 1 work order, so there is no one to evaluate for overload on it. For context, the only technicians with open work at MAIN:
- MECHTECH2 — 1 open (WO 1000046, Pump 3)
- HVACTECH1 — 1 open (WO 1000045, Chiller 6)

Nobody holds more than 5 → **no technician at MAIN is overloaded.**

## 4. TDCG from latest oil sample (2024‑01‑19)
H₂ 2,850 + CH₄ 7,400 + C₂H₆ 5,470 + C₂H₄ 16,650 + C₂H₂ 7 + CO 32 = **TDCG 32,409 ppm → Condition 4** (>4,630).
All six gases were non‑null in the latest sample — nothing carried forward.

## 5. Action taken
Transformer 1 is at Condition 4, so the reassignment branch applies — but **no reassignment was possible or performed**, because:
- The only open Transformer 1 WO (1000051) is not overdue and is not held by any technician, let alone an overloaded one.
- No technician at MAIN has any Transformer 1 history (the asset's only WO has never had labor assigned), so the eligible reassignment pool is empty.

**Least‑loaded technicians:** MECHTECH2 and HVACTECH1 (tied at 1 open WO each). Neither has transformer/OLTC history on record.

## Recommendation
Your premise doesn't hold — the urgent work isn't stuck behind an overloaded technician; it's stuck because **WO 1000051 has never been assigned or scheduled**. With TDCG at Condition 4 (roughly 7× the Condition 4 threshold) and a P1 rating, that's the real risk. I recommend:
1. **Bring in outside help** — an electrical/transformer specialist contractor for the OLTC inspection and lab DGA, since no in‑house tech has Transformer 1 history.
2. Schedule it **immediately**: the MAIN calendar has 0 scheduled WOs on every day from 2026‑09‑30 through 2026‑10‑07, so any day this week is clear.
3. If you'd like, I can assign MECHTECH2 or HVACTECH1 as the in‑house lead on 1000051 with a start date this week — just confirm which one, as I did not want to create a new assignment outside the rules you set.
